bib.title: Megatron-LM: Training Multi-Billion Parameter Language Models Using Model Parallelism

question: How can transformer language models with billions of parameters be trained with a simple intra-layer model parallel scheme in native PyTorch, and does the larger scale improve accuracy?
hypothesis: Larger transformer language models improve NLP accuracy, and layer-norm placement matters for BERT-like models as they scale.
contributions: A simple and efficient model parallel approach with only a few targeted modifications to an existing PyTorch transformer implementation.
In-depth empirical analysis of model and data parallel technique, up to 76% scaling efficiency using 512 GPUs.
Careful placement of layer normalization in BERT-like models is critical to increased accuracy as the model grows.
Scaling model size improves accuracy for GPT-2 (up to 8.3 billion) and BERT (up to 3.9B).
SOTA on WikiText103 (10.8 ppl), LAMBADA (66.5%) and RACE (90.9%).
Open-sourced code with training and evaluation pipelines.

method.summary: Intra-layer (tensor) model parallelism for transformers: the first MLP GEMM is split by columns and the second by rows, attention is split by heads, and the embedding is split along the vocabulary, needing two all-reduces in the forward and two in the backward pass per layer. Combined with data parallelism, GPT-2-style models up to 8.3B and BERT-style models up to 3.9B are trained on up to 512 V100 GPUs.

training.objective: GPT-2: left-to-right LM. BERT: masked LM with sentence order prediction instead of NSP and whole word n-gram masking
training.optimizer: Adam with weight decay; global gradient norm clipping 1.0
training.lr_schedule: GPT-2 single-cycle cosine decay over remaining 297k iterations; BERT linear decay over 2 million iterations
training.steps: GPT-2 300k iterations; BERT 2 million (336M, 1.3B), 1.5 million and still training (3.9B)
training.precision: mixed precision with dynamic loss scaling
training.regularisation: activation checkpointing after every transformer layer; weights init N(0, 0.02), residual-layer weights scaled by 1/sqrt(2N)
training.hardware: up to 32 DGX-2H servers, 512 Tesla V100 SXM3 32GB; 300 GB/s NVSwitch in server, 100 GB/s InfiniBand between servers (8 adapters per server)
training.wall_clock: one epoch (68,507 iterations) takes 0.86 / 2.27 / 2.10 days for 355M / 2.5B / 8.3B
training.seeds: BERT fine-tuning: median over 5 random seeds

other.finetune_hparams: Table 6, batch 16-256, lr 1e-5 to 5e-5, 2-12 epochs by task
other.scaling_study_batch: model parallel fixed batch 8; model+data parallel global batch 512 (64-way data parallel)

limits: Single-run results, no variance for pretraining; BERT fine-tuning uses median of 5 seeds.
3.9B BERT was still training when reported (1.5M of 2M iterations).
Layer-norm rearrangement shown only on BERT with loss curves (Fig 7) at 336M and 752M; no ablation table.
Models above 16B parameters would exceed one DGX-2H box; authors say hybrid intra-layer, inter-layer and inter-node parallelism is needed.
Optimizer state memory efficiency left to future work.
Tensor parallelism studied only up to 8-way, inside one server.
Efficiency measured on V100 with NVSwitch; 2019 hardware.
